question.prompt: Which of the following triangles cannot exist?

solutions.explanation:
A right triangle has one \(90^\circ\) angle. Its other two positive angles must therefore add to \(90^\circ\), so each is acute. Thus a right triangle cannot also have an obtuse angle.

The other combinations do occur. For A, B, D, and E, respective examples of angle triples are \((70^\circ,70^\circ,40^\circ)\), \((45^\circ,45^\circ,90^\circ)\), \((30^\circ,60^\circ,90^\circ)\), and \((20^\circ,40^\circ,120^\circ)\). Equal angles give equal opposite sides, while three different angles give three different sides.

The triangle that cannot exist is an obtuse right triangle, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
